title: Point Library .lup container
summary: A .lup is installable descriptive ZIP data: manifest.lus, catalog.json and verification.json. It declares operations bound to already installed tools, never code to execute. Installed in 1.1, it is a Luc: one bound to tools a library Luc of its own, one bound to code built into Lumeri a data layer on the Official Luc that holds that code (luc_cli.py convert). Governed Project registry storage is separate.

carrier.surface: ZIP .lup with manifest.lus, catalog.json and verification.json

replaceability.why: The .lup is descriptive data bound to existing tools; its parser never executes carried ZIP members.

reach.notes: Trusted Runtime seam, not an additional grant to a creator Luc.

operations.name: PointLibraryPackage.from_bytes

input.description: Draft JSON projection of native ZIP bytes.

operations.notes: No local operation deadline is enforced. Native API accepts bytes/bytearray; the JSON byte projection is draft. ZIP paths/duplicates/symlinks and sizes are checked. Main manifest/catalog/verification text is guarded and a declaration mapping is required; supplemental members are carried without execution.

invariants.text: ZIP members must have safe unique names, stay within accepted member prefixes and size bounds, and cannot be symlinks. Parsing never executes carried bytes.

A .lup bound to code built into Lumeri converts into a layer on the Official Luc that holds that code, carrying only its catalog and verification; switched off or taken away, the Official library answers again (Acrab, 2026-10-24). One that would be other code (name, shape, category, binding or tools) is refused.

break: An unhandled exception, invalid output, or failed declared artifact check.
failure.notes: A .lup converted into a layer on an Official library Luc is checked at load and read time; when refused, switched off, or taken away, Lumeri's own library answers again.

conformance.notes: Conversion into a layer and on/off/break fallback are held by tests/test_luc_library_layer.py.

known_deviations.text: Additional runtime/, ops/ and verification/ members are accepted as bytes. The text guard applies to manifest/catalog/verification, not every supplemental member; acceptance is not permission to execute them.
